rows.title: In GOP primary to replace Pete Olson, candidates seek to show they back Trump — and can win in a diverse district
rows.standfirst: Fifteen candidates — including a millionaire, a sheriff and a member of the Bush family — are vying for a spot in a near-certain runoff.

rows.title: Rice University asks “small group” to self-quarantine due to employee’s possible exposure to coronavirus
rows.standfirst: The Houston university said it’s making the move out of an abundance of caution.

rows.title: In two of Texas’ hottest primaries, it’s congressional clout versus ideological purity
rows.standfirst: Republican Kay Granger and Democrat Henry Cuellar excel at securing federal funding for their state, but they are beating back primary challenges from their parties’ insurgent wings.

rows.title: Patient with “weakly positive” test for coronavirus was released for a time in San Antonio
rows.standfirst: The person is back in quarantine, and health officials are tracking where they went.

rows.title: How do I participate in Libertarian or Green party primaries?
rows.standfirst: Members of the Green and Libertarian parties don’t participate in Super Tuesday. Instead, they choose candidates at conventions held over the course of the next few months.

rows.title: Analysis: Culling the Texas ballots, round one
rows.standfirst: Tuesday’s elections will trim dozens and dozens of would-be officeholders from the ballots, setting the table for a number of consequential runoffs and for a highly contested and anticipated general election in Texas.

rows.title: U.S. Supreme Court to hear Texas’ challenge to Obamacare
rows.standfirst: The high court is likely to take up the landmark health law for the third time this fall and issue a decision in 2021.

rows.title: T-Squared: The Texas Tribune, SXSW collaborating again on “Conversations about America’s Future”
rows.standfirst: Hillary Clinton, Will Hurd, Anita Hill, Gretchen Carlson, Adam Schiff, Kara Swisher, Andrew Yang and Robert Costa are among the participants in our two-day series of interviews and panel discussions on topics that affect us in Texas, the U.S. and around the world.

rows.title: San Antonio mayor demands extension of coronavirus quarantine, bans evacuees from entering city
rows.standfirst: Those moves — and an unsuccessful attempt to get an injunction against the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — came after a person who tested “weakly positive” for the new coronavirus was released over the weekend.

rows.title: UT-Austin announces updates to sexual misconduct policies after student protests
rows.standfirst: The school will make termination the “presumptive punishment” for employees who commit sexual assault or sexual harassment, among other offenses. It will also make available to the public information about those found responsible but not fired for such offenses.

rows.title: Trump administration awards $180 million for border barrier in Rio Grande Valley
rows.standfirst: The latest project will include a 30-foot-tall bollard wall, roads, lighting, cameras and other technology, Customs and Border Protection announced.

rows.title: They voted early for Buttigieg and Klobuchar in Texas. Now some feel they threw their votes away.
rows.standfirst: “We need ranked-choice voting,” said one Texas early voter who cast a ballot for Pete Buttigieg before he dropped out of the race.

rows.title: Analysis: As the Democratic old guard frets, Bernie Sanders finds a Texas foothold
rows.standfirst: Sanders’ success in Texas is an expression of a real change that, given the very demographics Democrats have been anticipating for years, will continue to shape the party’s electoral fortunes.

rows.title: Here’s how many coronavirus cases there are in Texas — and everything else you need to know
rows.standfirst: How many cases? Where are they? Who is most at risk? Here are the answers to questions about how the new strain of coronavirus is playing out in Texas.

rows.title: Alarm grows over coronavirus as thousands prepare to travel to Texas for SXSW and Houston rodeo
rows.standfirst: The March festival and other upcoming Texas events draw crowds from around the country and the world. But mounting fears around COVID-19 have some organizers canceling and attendees considering staying home.

rows.title: Joe Biden wins endorsements from Beto O’Rourke, other former rivals in late Texas surge
rows.standfirst: The former vice president received big-name endorsements — including backing from former presidential candidates Beto O’Rourke, Pete Buttigieg and Amy Klobuchar — as he campaigned in Dallas and Houston on the eve of Super Tuesday.

rows.title: Texas primary 2020 results: Watch live updates here
rows.standfirst: Get all of Texas’ election results through The Texas Tribune’s coverage of the 2020 primary races for president, U.S. Senate, U.S. House and the Texas Legislature.

rows.title: Five things to watch on Super Tuesday in Texas
rows.standfirst: There is a lot to monitor when the results come in Tuesday on primary election night. Here are five of the biggest things.

rows.title: Software updates slowing you down?
rows.standfirst: Texas A&M researchers, in collaboration with Intel Labs, have designed a tool that finds software update bugs in hours, not days.

rows.title: Coronavirus evacuees to be released from San Antonio quarantine Tuesday
rows.standfirst: Local officials said only people who have been symptom free for 14 days will be released from Lackland Air Force Base.

rows.title: Join The Texas Tribune and WFAA for election night results
rows.standfirst: We’re discussing election results with longtime partner WFAA-TV in Dallas as they come in Tuesday night. Join us starting at 6:55 p.m. Central Time.

rows.title: Three Texas House members are heading for runoffs
rows.standfirst: GOP state Reps. Dan Flynn and J.D. Sheffield will go into overtime rounds, as will state Rep. Harold Dutton, a Houston Democrat.

rows.title: MJ Hegar, Royce West head to runoff in Democratic primary to challenge U.S. Sen. John Cornyn
rows.standfirst: Through Tuesday night and much of Wednesday, Royce West and Cristina Tzintzún Ramirez were vying for the second-place finish that would get them into an overtime round with MJ Hegar.

rows.title: Joe Biden wins Texas primary in a stunning turnaround
rows.standfirst: Biden had trailed in the polls leading up to election day, which pointed to Bernie Sanders as the frontrunner.

rows.title: U.S. Reps. Kay Granger and Henry Cuellar claim victory in congressional primary races
rows.standfirst: Cuellar faced a challenge from attorney Jessica Cisneros, while Granger defeated former Colleyville City Council member Chris Putnam.

rows.title: Texas voting lines last hours after polls close on Super Tuesday
rows.standfirst: Voters in Houston, in Dallas and at Texas State University reported facing wait times that extended past two hours after polls closed.

rows.title: Incendiary State Board of Education candidate Rob Morrow advances to runoff
rows.standfirst: Neither party wants to see Morrow, who has a history of sexist and racist rhetoric, elected to the board, but he is headed to a runoff for the District 5 seat.

rows.title: Longtime Texas state Sen. Eddie Lucio Jr. heads to a runoff
rows.standfirst: The Brownsville Democrat has served in the Senate for nearly three decades. With all polling locations reporting Wednesday morning, he was just shy of the 50% vote mark needed to win outright.

rows.title: Did Pierce Bush’s family name doom his congressional run, or did his campaigning?
rows.standfirst: The grandson of the late President George H.W. Bush failed to make the runoff in a crowded GOP race to represent Texas’ 22nd District. Experts say the reasons are more complicated than the decline of the Bush family’s political influence.

rows.title: Railroad Commissioner Ryan Sitton concedes Republican primary in surprising upset
rows.standfirst: Sitton was elected in 2014 to the three-member board, which oversees Texas’ oil and gas industry. Jim Wright, who beat him in an upset, owns an oilfield waste services company.

rows.title: Baylor University’s focus on the future of Texas
rows.standfirst: Baylor University is experiencing a season of celebration and growth as the oldest continuously operating university in the state of Texas and one of the largest Christian research universities in the nation.

rows.title: In Texas, a chaotic primary yields status quo results
rows.standfirst: As Democrats and Republicans gear up for a competitive general election in Texas, there seems to be less appetite for intraparty warfare.

rows.title: Texas universities recall students, clean doorknobs as coronavirus safeguards
rows.standfirst: Students studying overseas are being brought home, and handshakes are discouraged as colleges and universities try to curtail coronavirus risks. No cases have been reported so far.

rows.title: TribCast: Joe Biden’s Super Tuesday win and other primary election results
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast — a supersized, live edition — Alexa talks to Ross, Patrick, Alex, Matthew, Cassi and Evan about Joe Biden’s Super Tuesday win and other notable primary election results.

rows.title: Analysis: Long lines, slow and error-filled counts. Why didn’t Tuesday night’s elections run better?
rows.standfirst: Super Tuesday in Texas exposed some problems in the state’s elections. Is this any way to run a model democracy?

rows.title: Joe Biden rode late momentum to Texas primary victory
rows.standfirst: The former vice president bested Bernie Sanders in Texas on the strength of election day ballots that heavily favored him in the state’s most populous counties.

rows.title: Bernie Sanders supporters in Texas are “pissed off.” But Texas Democrats need them in November.
rows.standfirst: “There’s been a lot of push against Sanders, and it makes me feel very helpless,” said one supporter. “There’s always going to be a faction of the party trying to stop him.”

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott asks 500,000 Texas educators to weigh in on preventing next school shooting
rows.standfirst: The survey on preparedness for active shooter situations and other crises will inform the largest needs assessment on school safety in Texas history.

rows.title: How do you solve a problem like Robert Morrow?
rows.standfirst: Despite his history of sexist, racist tweets and conspiracy-laden rants, more than 54,000 Republican voters propelled Robert Morrow into a runoff for a seat on the State Board of Education. GOP leaders are terrified he might actually win.

rows.title: Joe Biden to earn an estimated 111 of Texas’ Democratic primary delegates. Bernie Sanders will get 102.
rows.standfirst: The Texas Democratic Party released delegate counts Wednesday evening based on unofficial election results. Texas doles out 228 delegates in the state’s Democratic primary election.

rows.title: Texas man tests positive for coronavirus in Fort Bend County
rows.standfirst: Fort Bend Health and Human Services said the Houston-area man is in his 70s and recently traveled abroad.

rows.title: Harris County’s cascade of election day fumbles disproportionately affected communities of color
rows.standfirst: The last voters at Texas Southern University, a historically black university, ultimately spent nearly an entire workday waiting in line to cast their ballots, nearly seven hours after polls closed.

rows.title: A model that has laid the groundwork for other nonprofit journalism startups
rows.standfirst: The Texas Tribune has shared its insights about paying for journalism in the 21st century, and that has helped other nonprofit journalism outlets find a recipe for success.

rows.title: What can Texas do if a coronavirus outbreak hits?
rows.standfirst: While Texas has not yet seen “community spread” of coronavirus, U.S. health officials have told states to begin considering special measures in case of a COVID-19 outbreak.

rows.title: Texas lawmakers to hold hearing into excessive Super Tuesday voting lines
rows.standfirst: They also plan to address other issues at the hearing, including late-opening voting sites and insufficient voting equipment at polling places.

rows.title: A&M study: The future of Texas depends on climate preparedness
rows.standfirst: A study by five Aggie scientists indicates Texas should prepare for more extreme weather in the coming years — though it offers some glimmers of hope.

rows.title: Texas labs can now test for coronavirus, but capacity remains limited
rows.standfirst: The state lab in Austin can only test samples from up to 26 patients per day, while labs in Houston and El Paso can test up to 15 samples daily, officials said.

rows.title: Houston area has eight cases of coronavirus, all within a group of people who traveled overseas together
rows.standfirst: Officials have said there is no evidence of community spread in Texas and all the patients were exposed to the virus in Egypt.

rows.title: Texas Democrats sue the state to keep straight-ticket voting in 2020
rows.standfirst: In a federal lawsuit filed in Laredo, Democrats claim the move to end straight-ticket voting is unconstitutional and intentionally discriminates against Hispanic and black voters.

rows.title: Jerry McGinty to head troubled Legislative Budget Board
rows.standfirst: McGinty, the CFO of the Texas Department of Criminal Justice, will lead an embattled agency of nonpartisan budget analysts who have been without an executive director since October 2018.

rows.title: Harold Dutton: “It sounds like something criminal went on” in Texas House primary race
rows.standfirst: Facing a runoff, the Houston Democrat said he may ask the Harris County district attorney’s office to investigate the candidacy of an opponent who was seemingly absent on the campaign trail but received 20% of the vote.

rows.title: Democratic runoff to challenge Cornyn sets up crisp contrast between Hegar, West
rows.standfirst: After a 12-way primary, Texas Democrats get a chance to size up two candidates with very different pitches.

rows.title: In 2017, Texas leaders promised bold reforms to help child sex-trafficking victims. Here’s what’s changed — and what hasn’t.
rows.standfirst: State leaders have made serious reforms to some of the issues we previously reported on, though advocates say there’s still a long way to go.

rows.title: Just a quarter of registered voters in Texas participated in the 2020 presidential primary
rows.standfirst: More than 4 million Texans voted in the 2020 presidential primary election, with turnout among Democratic voters just barely surpassing Republican turnout.

rows.title: Experts say COVID-19 could hurt Texas trade and border economy
rows.standfirst: From cross-border trade with Mexico to oil and gas exports, Texas could soon start feeling economic impacts as the virus spreads and affects global supply chains, trade experts say.

rows.title: Harris County clerk apologizes to voters, “takes full responsibility” for long waits to vote in Houston
rows.standfirst: Some voters in Houston were stuck in excessively long lines and were forced to wait more than six hours to cast their ballots.

rows.title: Coronavirus concerns prompt Austin officials to cancel SXSW
rows.standfirst: Health officials have said there are no instances of the virus spreading within a Texas community. The annual Austin festival founded in 1987 attracts more than 400,000 attendees from all over the world and generates hundreds of millions of dollars.

rows.title: After 2018’s mass shooting, Santa Fe school officials will let some employees carry firearms at all times
rows.standfirst: District officials announced their plans Friday to implement Texas’ so-called Guardian Plan, which lets local school boards authorize specific employees to carry on campus at all times and determine their training standards.

rows.title: Texas seizes power from small East Texas school district, splitting town opinion
rows.standfirst: The Texas Education Agency announced a new appointed board and a new superintendent Friday for Shepherd Independent School District, where two schools failed to meet state academic standards for five years.

rows.title: UT-Arlington president announces resignation and looks for job in Florida
rows.standfirst: Vistasp Karbhari defended himself to the University of Central Florida against a pending lawsuit by calling it baseless.

rows.title: State Rep. Eddie Rodriguez becomes first to enter race for Senate District 14
rows.standfirst: Rodriguez, a longtime House Democrat from Austin, announced his candidacy Saturday for the seat being vacated by state Sen. Kirk Watson.

rows.title: Trump’s endorsements in Texas primary underscore his clout with GOP voters
rows.standfirst: The president’s support was most notable in five primaries Tuesday in which his preferred candidates all prevailed or advanced to a runoff.

rows.title: Dallas County asks for Super Tuesday recount after discovering it missed some ballots
rows.standfirst: In a petition filed late Friday in state district court, the county is seeking to perform a recount of backup paper ballots.

rows.title: More than 100 cruise ship passengers heading to San Antonio for coronavirus quarantine
rows.standfirst: Roughly 90 Texans are among the passengers heading to Lackland Air Force Base from a ship that had 21 confirmed cases of COVID-19. In Fort Bend County, officials have reported three new travel-related cases.

rows.title: Rice University canceling in-person classes after employee tested positive for novel coronavirus
rows.standfirst: It’s the first Texas university to issue major cancellations, which come after the number of Houston-area people who were exposed to the virus overseas continued to rise. There has been no known community spread in Texas, officials said.

rows.title: U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz says he “briefly interacted” with person who tested positive for coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Cruz, a Texas Republican, said he isn’t experiencing any symptoms and plans to stay at his Houston home until 14 days have passed since his brief interaction with the infected person.

rows.title: Texas Democrats are trying to draw LGBT Republicans snubbed by state GOP leaders
rows.standfirst: The Texas Republican party rejected Log Cabin Republicans asking to participate in the state convention. Democrats say they will work to recruit disillusioned LGBT conservatives. But Republicans aren’t worried about mass defections.

rows.title: Democratic male judges may be headed for extinction in Texas. The cause? Voters
rows.standfirst: Women got more votes than men in all of the roughly 30 gender-split primary contests for high court, court of appeals and district court. Rarely was it even close.

rows.title: U.S. markets crater as coronavirus-sparked oil war sends prices spiraling; trading suspended
rows.standfirst: The Dow plunges more than 1,900 points in a brutal global sell-off, and treasury yields dive to new lows, amplifying recession fears.

rows.title: Democrat suspends campaign after making runoff to challenge U.S. Rep. Dan Crenshaw
rows.standfirst: The move by Elisa Cardnell effectively hands her party’s nomination to Sima Ladjevardian, a Houston attorney and Democratic fundraiser backed by Beto O’Rourke.

rows.title: Texas coronavirus case confirmed in Collin County
rows.standfirst: The newest patient is a Frisco man in his 30s who recently traveled to California.

rows.title: Cristina Tzintzún Ramirez endorses Royce West over MJ Hegar in Democratic primary runoff for U.S. Senate
rows.standfirst: Tzintzún Ramirez finished closely behind West last week in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate.

rows.title: 12 Houston-area coronavirus cases linked to Egypt cruise
rows.standfirst: Another Harris County resident has tested positive for COVID-19. The individual was one of 17 Houston-area residents who recently traveled on the same Nile River cruise.

rows.title: How will collapsing oil prices affect Texas? It depends on these two factors, experts say.
rows.standfirst: A dramatic drop in oil prices over the weekend could harm Texas’ oil and gas industry and economy, but experts say it all depends on how long they remain low — and how the COVID-19 epidemic plays out.

rows.title: San Antonio mayor tries to calm coronavirus concerns but also says city needs more tests
rows.standfirst: Ron Nirenberg’s comment came as more people are set to be quarantined at Lackland Air Force Base. After criticizing health officials earlier this month, Nirenberg said the CDC has “made steps in the right direction” with how it oversees people who are quarantined.

rows.title: 5 million Texans lack health insurance. Here’s how that complicates the coronavirus response.
rows.standfirst: Texas has the highest share of uninsured residents of any state, with nearly 18% of people lacking health coverage, and many are unable to take paid sick leave from work. Experts say that makes it harder to contain an outbreak.

rows.title: Texas tried to take over Shepherd ISD. But a surprise, last-minute court order blocked those plans.
rows.standfirst: State officials were stopped from swearing in an appointed board of managers to run the East Texas school district where two schools received failing grades for years.

rows.title: New Texas coronavirus cases include Collin County child and a Montgomery County man whose travel is being investigated
rows.standfirst: The 3-year-old in Collin County is among the youngest patients in the U.S. to have tested positive for COVID-19, the disease caused by the new coronavirus. Montgomery County officials declined to comment on whether a patient there was exposed during travel.

rows.title: Judge allows Dallas County recount of missed ballots to move forward
rows.standfirst: Election officials discovered that an unknown number of votes weren’t counted on Super Tuesday. It’s unclear if any election outcomes might change when they are tabulated.

rows.title: Texas wants health insurers to waive costs of diagnosing the new coronavirus
rows.standfirst: “We must ensure no Texan is denied access to testing resources relating to coronavirus,” Gov. Greg Abbott said Tuesday.

rows.title: Coronavirus revives push for mandatory paid sick leave rules, but Texas leaders have long been opposed
rows.standfirst: Advocates argue that paid sick leave would allow workers to stay home and avoid spreading the deadly virus. Policies have been blocked in two Texas cities.

rows.title: “I did a horrible job,” House Speaker Dennis Bonnen says of meeting that led to his political downfall
rows.standfirst: Bonnen’s comments came during his first interview since announcing his retirement. The speaker also again defended his reasoning for taking the meeting.

rows.title: White House likely to pursue federal aid for shale companies hit by oil shock, coronavirus downturn
rows.standfirst: The idea could face resistance from those who support direct aid to workers. One critic called the idea ‘absurd.’

rows.title: Texas A&M cancels two days of classes to prepare for coronavirus
rows.standfirst: The College Station campus said it has no further plans to halt in-person instruction. The decision comes as universities across the country have begun moving classes online or switching to take-home exams, in response to the novel coronavirus.

rows.title: Travis County Judge Sarah Eckhardt resigns to run for Texas Senate
rows.standfirst: Eckhardt was elected Travis County’s first female county judge in 2015.

rows.title: New coronavirus evacuees have arrived at Lackland Air Force Base. What happens in Texas’ quarantine?
rows.standfirst: The San Antonio base has held hundreds of coronavirus evacuees. With about 100 more arriving Tuesday night and up to 120 more expected Wednesday, here’s what the quarantine site is like for those inside and outside the fence line.

rows.title: After messy primaries, local officials aim to up their game for November
rows.standfirst: It was largely human error and inexperience that caused massive lines and statewide vote miscounts during the March 3 primaries. Local election officials are trying to learn their lessons and avoid similar blunders in the general election.

rows.title: With six confirmed cases, panic in Fort Bend County spreading faster than the coronavirus
rows.standfirst: If there is an epicenter of the new coronavirus in Texas, it’s arguably Fort Bend County, which had the first confirmed case of COVID-19 outside of the federal quarantine site in San Antonio. There are six total cases there now, all stemming from an Egypt cruise trip.

rows.title: T-Squared: We’re pausing our in-person events, but we’ll be back soon. For now, we’re going virtual.
rows.standfirst: Fears about the coronavirus, real and existential, have resulted in many cancellations of crowded gatherings. Under the circumstances, and until things change, this is the prudent thing to do.

rows.title: Texans in Congress aim to contain coronavirus — and avoid contaminating each other
rows.standfirst: Nineteen of the 38 Texas members of Congress are over the age of 60, the age at which medical professionals say people are at most risk for serious complications from the virus.

rows.title: Texas’ first case of possible community spread of coronavirus highlights lack of testing
rows.standfirst: Officials said the patient attended a Feb. 28 barbecue at the popular Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo, though it’s unclear if he had symptoms at the time.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/11: UT-Austin closes sporting events to fans, Trump bans some inbound travel, and more
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Houston Rodeo called off as fears about new coronavirus continue to spread in Texas
rows.standfirst: It’s another devastating cultural and economic blow to a state that has confirmed more than 30 cases of the virus. Last year, the event drew more than 2.5 million attendees.

rows.title: Two Texas public school districts halt classes over possible coronavirus risks
rows.standfirst: The closures of Montgomery and Alvarado schools are short term, but hundreds of public school districts may face similar decisions. A big challenge for officials is figuring out how to feed low-income students in the event of prolonged shutdowns.

rows.title: Supreme Court says Trump administration may continue “remain in Mexico” policy
rows.standfirst: The justices reversed a decision by an appeals court that had ordered the policy be suspended on parts of the border.

rows.title: Dallas County recount turns up 9,149 new ballots but doesn’t swing any races
rows.standfirst: County officials asked for a redo of their vote count after discovering they missed ballots from 44 tabulating machines.

rows.title: TribCast: Coronavirus in Texas, a voting postmortem and Bonnen on his downfall
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Edgar, Matthew, Evan and Cassi about the status of the new coronavirus outbreak in Texas, Super Tuesday voting blunders and outgoing House Speaker Dennis Bonnen’s comments on his own downfall.

rows.title: Alleged bribes, kickbacks for law school admission at heart of Texas Southern University turmoil
rows.standfirst: An internal investigation found that unqualified students were admitted and given scholarships at Texas Southern’s law school and unearthed allegations of kickbacks to an admissions official. The incidents led to the ouster of university President Austin Lane.

rows.title: Texas Court of Criminal Appeals rejects new death penalty trial requested under “junk science” law
rows.standfirst: Rigoberto Avila Jr. was sentenced to death in 2001 in the death of his girlfriend’s 19-month-old son. In 2018, an El Paso judge recommended he get a new trial because of outdated science used at his trial.

rows.title: Texas colleges and universities are going online because of coronavirus. Here’s what they’re doing.
rows.standfirst: More than a dozen Texas schools are extending spring break and moving to online classes, at least temporarily. Some universities said they will cancel in-person instruction for the rest of the semester.

rows.title: Counting in Texas for the U.S. census has begun. Here’s what you need to know.
rows.standfirst: The accuracy of the count in the state will go a long way toward determining its economic, social and political future.

rows.title: All Republicans on State Board of Education endorse against Robert Morrow in runoff
rows.standfirst: Morrow faces Lani Popp, a Northside ISD speech language pathologist, in the May 26 runoff for an open seat on the board.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/12: Dallas-Fort Worth up to 13 cases, Houston area has 17
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: After updated results, Republican makes runoff for key state House seat by one-vote margin
rows.standfirst: Justin Berry advanced to the primary overtime round after earlier results had him missing the runoff by one vote. Third-place finisher Don Zimmerman has until Friday to request a recount.

rows.title: As coronavirus threat looms large over universities, UT president explains why his isn’t going online-only
rows.standfirst: In making the decision, UT prioritized on-time graduation and keeping the campus open for those who rely on it for accommodation and work, President Gregory Fenves said.

rows.title: School districts across Texas suspend classes over coronavirus concerns, prepare for online learning
rows.standfirst: Some of the districts extending their spring breaks are working on contingency plans to transition hundreds of thousands of students and teachers to remote learning in the event of even longer closures.

rows.title: Texans were already feeling coronavirus’ financial squeeze. Then the cases increased and cancellations mounted.
rows.standfirst: The state’s oil and gas industry has cratered. Major events have been called off, and tourism across Texas has dipped. It is too soon to tell the statewide economic impact from COVID-19, but Texans are already feeling a pinch.

rows.title: She’s a Texas nurse who treats cancer patients — and she can’t get a coronavirus test. That’s not unusual.
rows.standfirst: Unless a patient is sick enough to be hospitalized, state criteria for lab testing are difficult to meet. And state officials have yet to say how many Texans in total have been tested.

rows.title: Dallas County officials say community spread of coronavirus has occurred in North Texas
rows.standfirst: Officials made the announcement late Thursday. One out of five new cases disclosed in Dallas County came from someone who has no travel history.

rows.title: Michael Bloomberg promised to “help turn Texas blue.” Now some former employees and politicians are miffed that he’s fired his staff.
rows.standfirst: “Bloomberg was promising a long-term commitment to Texas regardless of who won the primary,” said one state representative. “It’s disappointing that with his defeat in the primary, the campaign has decided to reverse course.”

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/13: Shuttered schools can provide students’ lunches, Texas courts allowed to change deadlines
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Austin health officials say three people being treated for COVID-19; UT and Austin ISD schools close for the day
rows.standfirst: Two of those positive tests came from people living outside Travis County. Austin health officials said none of the cases are believed to be the result of community spread. UT-Austin’s president also said he is self-quarantining after his wife tested positive.

rows.title: T-Squared: How (and why) we’re covering the coronavirus in Texas
rows.standfirst: Coronavirus is in Texas, and The Texas Tribune is here to help — providing trusted information and helpful context about these rapidly changing events.

rows.title: Texas governor declares statewide emergency, says state will soon be able to test thousands
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott also announced drive-through testing capabilities in San Antonio, which could expand to Dallas, Houston and Austin in the coming weeks.

rows.title: Texas prisons, youth lockups cancel visitation after coronavirus disaster declaration
rows.standfirst: The Texas Department of Criminal Justice said no visitation would be allowed until further instruction Friday. Some county jails, like Harris and Dallas, have also halted visits.

rows.title: Texas politicians adjust campaigns amid coronavirus fears
rows.standfirst: “I think it would be hard to tell people that I’m out here running to make their lives better while at the same time putting their lives at risk,” said one state House candidate.

rows.title: In 2015, Texas lawmakers rejected effort to upgrade state’s disease response
rows.standfirst: After the Ebola outbreak, a task force recommended stockpiling protective gear and expanding state powers to deal with infectious diseases. “Tinfoil hats” opposed to big government killed a bill that would have done it, its sponsor says.

rows.title: Airlines prepare for uncertainty after European travel ban
rows.standfirst: Demand for airline travel rebounded quickly after outbreaks of swine flu, SARS and MERS. But the new coronavirus, so far, is less predictable. And it’s not clear when airlines can expect to recover after Trump’s European travel ban takes effect.

rows.title: Stop buying all the toilet paper. There’s no shortage if everyone takes only what they need.
rows.standfirst: State officials and industry representatives say Texans should relax: Stores plan to be stocked for months, so there’s no need to stockpile groceries and household items.

rows.title: Texas gets drive-thru coronavirus testing in San Antonio, but it’s not open to the general public
rows.standfirst: The drive-thru testing is not open to the general public, city officials said in a press release.

rows.title: Immigrant rights groups call on ICE to halt raids during coronavirus outbreak
rows.standfirst: A spokesperson for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said the agency does not conduct enforcement operations at medical facilities “except under extraordinary circumstances.”

rows.title: Shepherd ISD steps out of limbo and closer to state takeover
rows.standfirst: The East Texas district’s elected school board voted to drop any outstanding lawsuits blocking the state’s takeover of the district. Board members also ended a contract with lawyers involved in the dispute.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/14: Austin gets a drive-through testing center, H-E-B closing early
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Coronavirus community spread suspected in Brazoria County; patients attended Houston Rodeo
rows.standfirst: The individuals, who reside in the same household in Alvin, self-reported after going to the Houston Rodeo cook-off and livestock show and have not traveled outside the Houston area.

rows.title: Texas counties with coronavirus: Case updates and what we know
rows.standfirst: There are cases in each of the state’s five largest urban areas, though the virus has now also appeared in counties spanning from East Texas to the Gulf Coast. Officials expect statewide testing capacity to increase soon.

rows.title: Travelers stuck in long lines at DFW due to CDC questionnaire and enhanced screening, airport says
rows.standfirst: Many are returning following the travel ban announced by President Donald Trump, in which there’s a 30-day suspension of travel between Europe and the United State in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/15: Texas count climbs; state gets a boost in medical safety supplies
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: At Fort Worth church where the pastor has coronavirus, “thanks be to God” for Facebook Live
rows.standfirst: The building is closed, and some 40 members of the parish are in quarantine. They refuse to let that keep them apart.

rows.title: Many Texas schools could be closed through academic year due to coronavirus, education commissioner warns
rows.standfirst: In separate calls with superintendents and lawmakers Sunday, Texas Education Commissioner Mike Morath said decisions on extended school closures would be left up to locals.

rows.title: UT-Austin researcher explains lab’s key role in coronavirus vaccine development
rows.standfirst: We visited the University of Texas at Austin’s McLellan Lab, where scientists have made a critical breakthrough toward developing a vaccine for the 2019 novel coronavirus.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/16: Dallas, Houston closing bars; officials report at least 69 cases in state
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas STAAR test requirements waived due to coronavirus outbreak
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott also said he would ask the federal government to waive federal testing requirements, which apply to all states.

rows.title: Watch Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s press conference on coronavirus updates
rows.standfirst: On Friday, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott declared a statewide public health disaster and said Texas would soon be able to ramp up testing for the new coronavirus.

rows.title: Texan Louie Gohmert backs off from challenge to federal coronavirus package
rows.standfirst: Several reports had suggested that Gohmert could have delayed the bill’s passage by days.

rows.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott says to expect “exponential” increase in positive coronavirus cases
rows.standfirst: As the virus that causes COVID-19 increasingly spreads through Texas communities and the state’s testing capacity increases, the number of positive cases will rise.

rows.title: Texas Court of Criminal Appeals stops an execution because of coronavirus
rows.standfirst: John Hummel’s lawyer requested a stay of execution in a unique court filing Friday, but Tarrant County officials opposed it.

rows.title: Degrees of anxiety: As college classrooms empty, students fear for educations, jobs
rows.standfirst: Texas universities are moving online, but how do you learn circuit welding or vocal ensemble by videoconference? What happens when campus jobs dry up? And will anyone get to walk the stage come graduation day?

rows.title: Coronavirus prompts Dallas and Houston to close bars and clubs, make restaurants takeout only
rows.standfirst: Restaurants in Dallas and Harris counties for now may remain open for drive-through, takeout and delivery, but dine-in service will be prohibited.

rows.title: Amid coronavirus concerns, Justice Department continues “remain in Mexico” hearings in immigration courts
rows.standfirst: It was business as usual Monday on the Migrant Protection Protocols docket in federal immigration courts, and groups that work in them are raising concerns about the risk to migrants and court staff.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott postpones special Texas Senate election due to coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: The special election is now set for July 14.

rows.title: Texas officials link man’s death to coronavirus, first such case in state
rows.standfirst: The man, in his late 90s, had symptoms consistent with the new coronavirus, and a test later came back positive for COVID-19, officials said.

rows.title: For Texas’ ill and immunocompromised, coronavirus brings a new threat and familiar precautions
rows.standfirst: “We are perpetually at risk,” said Shelby Chiles of Lewisville, who has a rare autoimmune disease.

rows.title: Coronavirus derails ground game for Texas census count
rows.standfirst: Years of work went into planning neighborhood canvasses and educational efforts to reach out to every Texan, especially those most likely to be missed in the tally. Now those efforts are down for the count.

rows.title: While other states fighting coronavirus enforce widespread closures, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott goes with a patchwork system
rows.standfirst: While most states have mandated the closure of schools, bars and restaurants; deployed their militaries; or diverted state resources to COVID-19 response, Texas is largely leaving it up to schools and local governments to decide how to proceed. Some say the approach can undermine response efforts.

rows.title: Social distancing has upended the financial lives of countless Texans. And many don’t know what’s next.
rows.standfirst: Officials say they have to prioritize public health over economic concerns. Meanwhile, people who can’t work from home navigate a public health crisis while facing financial uncertainty.

rows.title: Texans still clamoring for coronavirus tests as state promises availability will skyrocket
rows.standfirst: Texas appears to be lagging behind other populous states in testing for COVID-19, but trying to determine how many tests have been given is as confusing as figuring out how to get one.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/17: Feds consider sending people economic stimulus checks; state has more than 70 known cases
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas coronavirus cases prompt Gov. Greg Abbott to activate National Guard
rows.standfirst: Abbott said that National Guard troops, if deployed, could do things like help with traffic at drive-through testing sites.

rows.title: Austin joins other major cities shuttering bars, entertainment venues and in-house restaurant service
rows.standfirst: The move, which follows similar shutdowns in Dallas and Harris County, also limits gatherings of more than 10 people.

rows.title: Texas hospitals don’t have enough beds for coronavirus patients if too many people get sick at once
rows.standfirst: Texas has about 2.9 hospital beds per 1,000 people — less than one-fourth the rate of South Korea.

rows.title: As coronavirus stops people from gathering, Gov. Greg Abbott suspends part of open-meetings law
rows.standfirst: All sections of the Texas Open Meetings Act remain in place except for the requirement of a physical gathering space for people to watch the meeting and ask questions.

rows.title: Texas parents struggle to find child care, food as school closings keep kids at home
rows.standfirst: Lower-income households are being hit the hardest by school closings as parents try to hang on to jobs and care for their children. Districts are cobbling together ways to keep their educations on track.

rows.title: Are hospitals near me ready for coronavirus? Here are nine different scenarios.
rows.standfirst: How soon regions run out of hospital beds depends on how fast the novel coronavirus spreads and how many open beds they had to begin with. Here’s a look at the whole country. You can also search for regions in Texas.

rows.title: UT, A&M among Texas colleges postponing graduation ceremonies and moving classes online for the semester
rows.standfirst: The announcements are among the latest responses to the novel coronavirus. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recently recommended canceling gatherings with 50 or more people for the next eight weeks.

rows.title: How many Texans have been tested for the new coronavirus? State data is incomplete. But here’s what we know.
rows.standfirst: The state isn’t reporting tests conducted by some hospitals and private labs. But the figures available show that Texas could be lagging behind other states. Officials say that’s because the virus showed up elsewhere earlier.

rows.title: Texas death linked to coronavirus came from community spread in retirement home
rows.standfirst: All residents of the retirement community will be tested, Gov. Greg Abbott said Wednesday.

rows.title: Staying home slows the coronavirus, but what if you’re homeless?
rows.standfirst: Local, state and national leaders are recommending people take a range of actions to protect themselves from the new coronavirus. But for those without homes, many of those measures are next to impossible.

rows.title: Four former rivals endorse Pete Sessions in runoff to replace U.S. Rep. Bill Flores
rows.standfirst: The group includes George Hindman, who narrowly missed the runoff in the 12-way March 3 primary.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/18: Tech student with coronavirus violated quarantine protocols, officials say
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Coronavirus outbreak could postpone Texas municipal elections until November
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott has yet to issue guidance on the May 26 runoff election.

rows.title: Collin County man’s death marks third Texas fatality from new coronavirus
rows.standfirst: This is is the second death in North Texas related to COVID-19.

rows.title: TribCast: Texas’ growing response to coronavirus amid a growing outbreak
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast — a different format in the time of the new coronavirus — Alexa talks to Edgar and Aliyya about the state’s response to a growing outbreak, an assessment of hospital capacity and the impact of school district closures.

rows.title: What we know about coronavirus testing in Texas
rows.standfirst: Even as demand for testing has increased, public and federal labs continue to prioritize Texans who meet certain criteria.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott on Texas bars and restaurants: Expect an announcement Thursday
rows.standfirst: “We’re dealing with something … that is not just statewide in scope, not just nationwide in scope, but is worldwide in scope,” Abbott said.

rows.title: Texas lets school districts decide whether students can graduate without STAAR
rows.standfirst: The state standardized test, taken in third through 12th grade, determines whether students can graduate or move on to the next grade and whether schools can stay open.

rows.title: Texas universities ramp up online teaching amid coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: Professors and instructors are polishing their technical skills — with a little trepidation among technological Luddites — as Texas colleges move courses online. The transition is marked by uncertainty, including over how courses like labs and art can be taught virtually.

rows.title: Texas transit agencies are still getting front-line responders and low-income Texans to work. But service may change as the crisis continues.
rows.standfirst: Leaders in the Austin, Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston and San Antonio areas are already analyzing how fewer fares and drops in sales tax will affect them.

rows.title: ICE to stop most immigration enforcement inside United States, will focus on criminals during coronavirus outbreak
rows.standfirst: The shift comes amid the deepening global coronavirus crisis.

rows.title: Government guidelines urge people to work from home. So why are government workers required to come to the office?
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump issued guidelines suggesting people avoid groups larger than 10 people. Last week, Gov. Greg Abbott directed state agencies to provide flexible and remote work options to employees. But many government workers still don’t have the option.

rows.title: U.S. Sen. John Cornyn draws rebuke for blaming coronavirus on China
rows.standfirst: The Republican Texas senator alluded to a now-debunked myth that the outbreak began after a woman ate bat soup. And he incorrectly cited China as the birthplace of two previous outbreaks.

rows.title: “It’s going to hurt”: New coronavirus shocks Texas economy as length of public health crisis remains unknown
rows.standfirst: The novel coronavirus has caught governments unprepared, put people out of work and set businesses on the brink of closure. Congress is working on a federal stimulus package as unemployment claims in Texas are expected to rise.

rows.title: Texas is urging patients to seek remote health care. Some insurance plans won’t pay for it.
rows.standfirst: As millions of Texans isolate themselves in an attempt to limit the spread of COVID-19, state officials are working to ramp up the use of telemedicine. But many health plans are outside of their regulatory authority.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/19: Supreme Court halts evictions statewide
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas Court of Criminal Appeals stops another scheduled execution because of the coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Tracy Beatty requested the court stay his execution, set for next week, after the court halted this week’s execution.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott give an update on Texas’ efforts to combat coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Watch a livestream of the Texas governor discussing everything the state is doing to limit the spread of COVID-19, the disease caused by the new coronavirus. The address is scheduled to start at noon Central Time.

rows.title: Coronavirus pauses many Texas court proceedings. For some, that means more time in jail.
rows.standfirst: Courts have slowed across the state, and jury trials are on hold. Defense attorneys worry the outbreak could leave their clients sitting in jail waiting for justice — and vulnerable to catching the virus.

rows.title: Houston-area nursing home resident and Dallas man in his 60s die from coronavirus
rows.standfirst: There were a total of five reported deaths in Texas related to COVID-19 as of Thursday.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott closes bars, restaurants and schools as he anticipates tens of thousands could test positive for coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Abbott disclosed that estimate hours after he took sweeping action to stop the virus’ spread.

rows.title: Houston has a new drive-through coronavirus test site, but three others can’t open due to shortages
rows.standfirst: Mayor Sylvester Turner said a lack of personal protective equipment for health workers is one reason three sites in Houston and Harris County can’t open yet. Long lines formed at the one that did.

rows.title: Texas regulators contemplating a reduction in oil production amid coronavirus crisis
rows.standfirst: A Texas Railroad Commission official said no decision has been made yet and the agency is looking into options.

rows.title: Coronavirus testing ramps up in Texas, but more is needed
rows.standfirst: Experts said the state’s testing capability wasn’t where it needed to be to measure how effective efforts to contain the virus have been or where the outbreak is on its trajectory toward peaking.

rows.title: Calls for Trump administration to release migrants from detention increase amid COVID-19 pandemic
rows.standfirst: Fear and anxiety within the immigrant community is spreading as detainees fear an outbreak of the new coronavirus in detention facilities.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/20: More than 5,000 tests given, 212 test positive
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: T-Squared: Meet the newest members of our investigative partnership
rows.standfirst: Our new engagement reporter, research reporter, data reporter and development lead will help us immensely as we work to bring a new level of watchdog journalism to Texas.

rows.title: Texas appeals court lets controversial illegal voting conviction stand
rows.standfirst: In a rare voting fraud case, Crystal Mason was sentenced to five years in prison for casting a provisional ballot in 2016 while on supervised release for a federal felony. She says she did it on the advice of a poll worker.

rows.title: To slow COVID-19, Trump administration closes southern border to nonessential travel
rows.standfirst: The border will be closed for all crossings other than commercial trade and specified reasons such as medical care and education.

rows.title: Texas restaurants are asking for tax relief from the state. But officials say they need those revenues during the pandemic.
rows.standfirst: Restaurant owners say that delaying sales tax payments could help them ride out the pandemic. State officials, however, say that those revenues help keep hospitals and emergency services running.

rows.title: Small businesses in Texas can apply for emergency federal loans to help ride out coronavirus pandemic, Abbott announces
rows.standfirst: Texans can apply online to see if they qualify for a long-term, low-interest loan from the U.S. Small Business Administration.

rows.title: Patients face canceled appointments and delayed surgeries as doctors respond to coronavirus. They’re worried about the wait.
rows.standfirst: On Friday, several major health care providers announced they would postpone elective surgeries and other non-urgent procedures and appointments.

rows.title: Citing coronavirus threat, Texas Democrats sue to expand mail-in voting
rows.standfirst: The Democratic Party wants a judge to declare the novel coronavirus a circumstance that allows anyone to request a mail-in ballot. The GOP has opposed expanding the state’s limited absentee voting rules.

rows.title: Texas delaying May primary runoff elections in response to coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott on Friday postponed the May 26 runoff election to July under the emergency powers of his previous statewide disaster declaration.

rows.title: As coronavirus sparks rumors, Houston officials dispel social media myth of a citywide lockdown
rows.standfirst: Officials say they’re investigating whoever is behind the misinformation campaign, which they say only creates anxiety and fear.

rows.title: “Unsupported and ignored”: Texans stuck in Peru say their government abandoned them
rows.standfirst: Texans marooned there after the country closed its borders described a harrowing ordeal trying to find a plane ticket out. The U.S. government is trying to repatriate them.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/21: At least 325 cases reported in state; Gov. Greg Abbott moves to bolster number of practicing nurses
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Four COVID-19 cases reported at North Texas facility for people with disabilities
rows.standfirst: Three of the residents are in their 60s and another is in their 50s, officials said, and all have been hospitalized.

rows.title: Travel restrictions at U.S.-Mexico border have area businesses grappling with uncertainty
rows.standfirst: The potential collapse of cross-border commerce has added border store owners to the ranks of Texas restaurateurs and other small businesses who don’t know how they’ll be able to make ends meet.

rows.title: Dallas County bans elective medical procedures to focus resources on climbing coronavirus cases
rows.standfirst: Dallas County Judge Clay Jenkins’ order, which runs through April 3, came the same day Gov. Greg Abbott sought to increase the state’s number of practicing nurses.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/22: Gov. Greg Abbott says Texas has 566 cases; state’s number of deaths at 7
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott resists calls for statewide shelter-in-place; moves to expand hospital capacity
rows.standfirst: Abbott said he would applaud some local authorities for issuing such an order, while he would remain flexible on strategies as the new coronavirus continues to spread.

rows.title: Dallas County orders residents to shelter in place as coronavirus cases there spread
rows.standfirst: Dallas County Judge Clay Jenkins’ new order came after Gov. Greg Abbott held off from issuing a similar directive to the entire state.

rows.title: Analysis: Order Texans to stay home, or risk impeding the fight against COVID-19?
rows.standfirst: Health experts and local leaders want stricter state orders to keep Texans at home, but for now, Gov. Greg Abbott is leaving the decisions on “shelter-in-place” to local officials.

rows.title: Immigration attorneys worry ICE rules will take away needed medical supplies
rows.standfirst: Immigration and Customs Enforcement is requiring lawyers to wear personal protective equipment to detention facilities. That could keep the equipment out of the hands of medical personnel — or make it harder for lawyers to see their clients, some say.

rows.title: Texas’ budget could take massive hit as coronavirus crisis continues unfolding, lawmakers learn
rows.standfirst: Texas Comptroller Glenn Hegar told House members that it’s too soon to make detailed forecasts, but both the state budget and Economic Stabilization Fund could be drastically revised down.

rows.title: As coronavirus spreads, some Asian Americans worry their leaders’ language stokes a stigma
rows.standfirst: “If the virus has already been named by the [World Health Organization] as COVID-19, any renaming is highly politically charged and motivated,” said one researcher.

rows.title: How to help — and find help — as the coronavirus surges in Texas during the holiday season
rows.standfirst: Food banks and nonprofits are providing free meals, internet access and housing assistance. As they face an increase in demand during another coronavirus surge, the organizations are also asking for help.

rows.title: No abortions in Texas unless the mother’s life is in danger, Texas attorney general says as coronavirus spreads
rows.standfirst: The warning comes one day after Gov. Greg Abbott ordered health care facilities and professionals to postpone all procedures that are deemed “not medically necessary” as the state gears up for an influx of patients with COVID-19.

rows.title: Texas’ largest counties are issuing stay-at-home orders as coronavirus spreads
rows.standfirst: The orders represent some of the most stringent measures local officials in Texas have taken so far to address the colossal public health crisis.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/23: No room for tourists in Jeff Davis County
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Police across Texas are enforcing social distancing, but they’re hesitant to make arrests
rows.standfirst: Law enforcement agencies are focusing instead on education or issuing warnings.

rows.title: Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick says a failing economy is worse than coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick told Fox News on Monday that he would rather perish from the new coronavirus than see the economy destroyed for his grandchildren by overreaction to the disease.

rows.title: Four former Bloomberg workers in Texas claim he reneged on pay promise
rows.standfirst: The Texas lawsuits surfaced as the former Democratic presidential candidate faces a growing uproar from staffers he laid off en masse after dropping out of the race earlier this month.

rows.title: Rural Texas hospitals should be staffing up to face coronavirus. Many can’t afford to.
rows.standfirst: Public health precautions undertaken to slow the spread of COVID-19, such as the cancellation of more lucrative elective surgeries, will hit rural hospitals especially hard, administrators say.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/24: Quarantine ending for cruise ship evacuees at Lackland Air Force Base
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Travis County Judge Sarah Eckhardt pushes back resignation to focus on coronavirus response
rows.standfirst: Eckhardt had been planning to resign to run for state Senate. Now she says she’ll stay on until mid-May.

rows.title: Grocery workers are risking their health during the pandemic to keep stores open. They want better pay and protections.
rows.standfirst: Union members are advocating for government benefits like priority child care and better access to testing. Workers also want hazard pay and expanded sick leave policies.

rows.title: Analysis: Coronavirus, family, economics and false choices
rows.standfirst: The threat to the economy is important, but it’s also secondary. The worst of the new coronavirus has not yet been visited upon us.

rows.title: Texas unemployment rate headed toward double digits, comptroller warns
rows.standfirst: Texas reported a record low unemployment rate of 3.5% in January. The historic high was 9.2% in 1986.

rows.title: Denton County asks state for temporary hospital after COVID-19 outbreak at state supported living center
rows.standfirst: Denton’s mayor and the county judge are pleading with Gov. Greg Abbott for an on-site hospital after six residents of the Denton State Supported Living Center, which has more than 1,800 residents and staff members, tested positive for the virus.

rows.title: Worried about current compliance, Gov. Greg Abbott signals openness to stricter coronavirus order
rows.standfirst: “It’s clear to me that we may not be achieving the level of compliance that is needed,” Abbott said during a news conference in Austin.

rows.title: Coronavirus hits Texas prisons with first inmate case confirmed
rows.standfirst: The 37-year-old man has been isolated and is being treated at the prison system’s Galveston hospital, where he’s been for three days.

rows.title: Texas day cares are closing just when some parents need them more than ever
rows.standfirst: The new coronavirus has prompted parents to pull their kids from day care, and thousands have closed. But essential workers like nurses, police officers and grocery store clerks desperately need safe places to leave their children.

rows.title: How many coronavirus cases in Texas? Depends on who you ask
rows.standfirst: On Tuesday evening, Texas launched a new system for reporting cases of COVID-19. Officials said the new system will bring the state’s count closer to those of counties and other sources that were reporting hundreds more cases.

rows.title: TribCast: How coronavirus is affecting Texas workers, immigrants and the courts
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast — a different format in the time of the new coronavirus — Alexa talks to Mitchell, Julián and Jolie about rising unemployment in Texas, the outbreak’s effect on immigrants and delayed justice in the court system.

rows.title: Texas schools get OK to give free meals to parents when kids aren’t present
rows.standfirst: Federal officials had previously approved a waiver allowing school districts to hand out curbside breakfasts and lunches to parents who show up. Now districts have more flexibility on how and what they feed students in free and reduced-price meals while schools are temporarily closed statewide.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/25: Unemployment claims surge
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas hospitals brace for coronavirus surge with uncertain stocks of protective gear
rows.standfirst: “’I will give you X number, you are to make these last for however long,’” a Panhandle hospital executive told one of his clinics when it sought more respirators. “We’ve got to ration these resources.”

rows.title: Texas cancels controversial Medicaid contracts after complaints of subjective scoring
rows.standfirst: “This decision is necessary to ensure the contract award processes are conducted with integrity, fairness and transparency,” a spokeswoman for the Texas Health and Human Services Commission said.

rows.title: Texas hospitals plan to add beds, eye vacated buildings as they prepare for a possible influx in coronavirus cases
rows.standfirst: The efforts to quickly add capacity come after Gov. Greg Abbott waived hospitals’ occupancy restrictions Sunday and ordered health care providers to postpone surgeries that are not “immediately, medically necessary.”

rows.title: Abortion providers sue Texas over coronavirus-related order
rows.standfirst: Attorney General Ken Paxton said this week that abortions should not be performed unless the mother’s life is in danger, saying health care capacity needs to be preserved for COVID-19 patients.

rows.title: Migrants say COVID-19 fears led to disturbance in Texas immigration detention center
rows.standfirst: About 60 detainees in the South Texas ICE Processing Center staged an uprising this week. Some detainees say fear of infection sparked the incident; Immigration and Customs Enforcement disputes that account.

rows.title: Coronavirus is officially in Texas prisons and jails. Now what?
rows.standfirst: The Texas prison system and Dallas County both reported the first Texas cases of inmates testing positive for the new coronavirus this week. Self-quarantines and social distancing aren’t always possible for those who’ve been exposed.

rows.title: Texas campaigns prepare for more uncertainty after runoff reset by coronavirus
rows.standfirst: With the runoff date pushed back seven weeks, the coronavirus pandemic continues to cast a long shadow over Texas politics.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/26: U.S. Rep. Lizzie Fletcher moves to self-quarantine
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: The number of Texans filing for unemployment increased 860% in a week
rows.standfirst: Two weeks ago, 16,176 Texans filed for new unemployment benefits. But just one week later — after leaders shut down businesses across the state to slow the spread of the new coronavirus — that number jumped up to 155,657 out-of-work people filing for unemployment relief.

rows.title: Watch Texas Gov. Greg Abbott provide a coronavirus update
rows.standfirst: Abbott is set to provide an update on the state’s response to the new coronavirus at 2 p.m. in Austin. He’ll be joined by the commissioner of the Texas Department of State Health Services and the head of the Texas Division of Emergency Management.

rows.title: A quilter, a chocolate maker and a man on a mission: Meet the Texans improvising masks for doctors
rows.standfirst: In fabric shops and on factory floors, the race is on to make and manufacture personal protective equipment in Texas before supplies run out for those on the front lines of the coronavirus outbreak.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott orders air travelers from New Orleans and around New York to self-quarantine
rows.standfirst: The order aligns Texas with federal guidance announced Wednesday that aims to contain the spread of the virus outside New York, which has become the epicenter of the outbreak in the United States.

rows.title: Texas regulators vote to ban residential utility shut-offs during pandemic while buoying companies
rows.standfirst: The Texas Public Utility Commission approved an order Thursday that would ban disconnections of water and power service for Texans financially impacted by COVID-19 and put them on deferred payment plans. But advocates and experts say the real winner might be utility providers.

rows.title: Hidalgo County breaks out the megaphones in scramble to salvage census push
rows.standfirst: Coaxing census participation was going to be hard enough in some of Texas’ poorest communities. With coronavirus restrictions, organizers turned to driving sound trucks around colonias on the border, but now even that won’t be possible.

rows.title: Is Cabela’s an “essential” business? Texas counties differ on who should work during shelter in place
rows.standfirst: With Gov. Greg Abbott resisting calls for a statewide stay-at-home order, local officials are tasked with deciding which businesses and employees are essential. This strategy means the rules differ from county to county, and many employees are confused about why they’re being called in to work.

rows.title: Texas’ shuttered businesses, laid-off workers and overwhelmed hospitals among beneficiaries of coronavirus relief bill
rows.standfirst: The historic legislation, worth more than $2 trillion, heads to the U.S. House on Friday after the Senate passed it unanimously.

rows.title: Dallas County creating temporary hospital, calls in National Guard for medical help as novel coronavirus cases top 300
rows.standfirst: The North Texas county leads the state in the number of novel coronavirus cases and is marshaling resources as the need for medical response grows.

rows.title: Caught between local officials and Donald Trump, Gov. Greg Abbott carefully navigates coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Abbott’s approach has helped keep the peace across levels of government handling the response in Texas but has also raised questions about whether he’s being aggressive enough in responding to a virus that threatens thousands of lives.

rows.title: Analysis: Coronavirus and local control in Texas
rows.standfirst: Without broader statewide orders for Texans to stay at home, local officials — and local circumstances — have made the state a patchwork of responses to the new coronavirus.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/27: U.S. House approves coronavirus spending bill
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: St. Mary’s University School of Law professor champions civil rights, education issues
rows.standfirst: As he approached the bench, Albert Kauffman, J.D., knew this case would be an uphill battle.

rows.title: Out of sight, child abuse in Texas thought to be on the rise
rows.standfirst: Families are stuck at home, confronting stress and fear. And with many schools and day care centers shuttered, child welfare workers can’t rely on teachers to help detect abuse.

rows.title: Why the 2020 census is as important as ever
rows.standfirst: Even with COVID-19 upending our lives, communities still need to be counted.

rows.title: Texas gun stores are essential businesses, may stay open during the pandemic, attorney general says
rows.standfirst: City and county officials cannot prohibit the sale of guns during an emergency declaration, according to the Texas Attorney General.

rows.title: Many Texans in Congress scrambled to join vote as U.S. House passes coronavirus spending bill
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump is expected to sign the bill into law.

rows.title: Citing coronavirus pandemic, Trump administration stops enforcing environmental laws
rows.standfirst: A Texas environmental protection group said it is “reckless” for the Environmental Protection Agency to waive enforcement of many protections. The federal agency said companies could have trouble complying due to the new coronavirus.

rows.title: Coronavirus cases surge to 39 at living facility for Texans with intellectual and developmental disabilities
rows.standfirst: The center serves more than 400 people with disabilities and it employees about 1,400 staff members.

rows.title: Another small business reeling from COVID-19: the doctor’s office
rows.standfirst: Primary care doctors are warning that if they have to close, more patients might end up in Texas hospitals at a time when those facilities don’t have the capacity to handle them.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/28: SNAP and Medicaid coverage in Texas extended
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Coronavirus test results in Texas are taking up to 10 days
rows.standfirst: Though Texas has dramatically increased its testing capacity, many who have gotten one are waiting days on end, and sometimes a week or more, for the results, according to interviews with patients and health care professionals.

rows.title: Midland confronts coronavirus after oil prices plummet
rows.standfirst: The city’s new mayor is struggling to inspire in a moment of overlapping crises.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/29: Harris County jail inmate tests positive
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for updates.

rows.title: Texas expands travel restrictions, launches pop-up hospital as coronavirus spreads
rows.standfirst: In Texas, Abbott said the state’s first ad hoc health care facility to respond to the pandemic will be the Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center in Dallas, an original hotspot for the outbreak at the state level.

rows.title: As local officials shrink jail populations due to coronavirus, Abbott blocks release of some inmates who can’t pay bail
rows.standfirst: Abbott’s order bans release without paying bail for inmates who are accused of or have been convicted in the past of violent offenses. Defendants with cash could still walk free.

rows.title: Analysis: A Texas governor caught betwixt and between Texas attitudes
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott has been slow to impose statewide stay-at-home orders, a reluctance mirrored in many of the state’s cities and counties. But more are issuing advisories as the new coronavirus pandemic spreads in Texas.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/30: Cases emerge at second state-run home for disabled
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas A&M telehealth services hold potential to slow COVID-19 spread.
rows.standfirst: Assessing COVID-19 patients through telehealth services, like those offered by Texas A&M’s Telebehavioral Care program, can help health care providers treat isolated patients and prevent the spread of the virus.

rows.title: Older inmates sue Texas prison system over coronavirus policies and practices
rows.standfirst: The Texas Department of Criminal Justice’s measures to combat the new coronavirus are insufficient at a geriatric prison, the complaint said.

rows.title: Federal judge temporarily blocks Texas’ ban on abortions during coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: The court granted abortion providers’ motion to temporarily block the state from enforcing the order, which was set to expire April 21, as it relates to abortions.

rows.title: Texas shale producers ask state to cut oil output as demand plummets during coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: Two Texas oil companies with big business in the Permian Basin wrote to state regulators requesting an emergency meeting to consider reducing oil production as demand around the world has collapsed due to the new coronavirus.

rows.title: Under coronavirus immigration measures, U.S. is expelling border-crossers to Mexico in an average of 96 minutes
rows.standfirst: The pandemic has allowed the U.S. Border Patrol to implement the kind of rapid-fire deportation system President Donald Trump has long extolled as his preferred approach.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 3/31: State reports 3,266 cases and 41 deaths; Paxton gets temporary victory on abortion ban
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Someone says they have 2 million N95 masks for sale. The asking price is six times the usual cost.
rows.standfirst: As health care professionals beg for supplies to protect themselves from COVID-19 infection, a Texas company found a seller with at least 2 million masks and quietly offered them for sale at $6 each. Before the pandemic, they cost around $1.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott give the latest on Texas’ efforts to combat coronavirus
rows.standfirst: State health and education officials will join Abbott at 2 p.m. Central Time on Tuesday for an update on efforts to limit the spread of COVID-19, the disease caused by the new coronavirus.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott tells Texans to stay home except for essential activity in April
rows.standfirst: He also said that schools would remain closed until at least May 4 as the state increases its efforts to stop the spread of the new coronavirus.

rows.title: Harris County’s misdemeanor judges won’t follow Abbott’s order limiting jail releases during coronavirus
rows.standfirst: The judges are under a federal court order to release low-level defendants without collecting bail payment after the county’s cash bail practices were found unconstitutional. The governor’s Sunday order does not allow those accused of low-level crimes to leave jail without access to cash if they have a past violent conviction.
